??? quote "Dialogue"

    - The middle verse is in my coat pocket, in Piper's hand. I read it every morning before the tragedies. Do not tell anybody about the tragedies. Everybody knows. Do not tell them.
    - One speech, Dina in the back row, and no bow. I have been practising not bowing. It is the hardest thing I have ever done.
    - What can the grandee do for you, *Player*? Within reason. Outside reason costs extra.
        - *Choice:* Tell me about the grandee.
        - *Choice:* How did you get the part?
        - *Choice:* Tell me about Sprout.
        - *Choice:* Nothing, thanks.
    - A puffed-up worthy of Selsior who bans everything fun. Music! Banned. Dancing! Banned. Laughing at grandees! Especially banned. He falls off things, and in the end the market crowd chases him off the cart.
    - And the hat: a tower of purple felt and feathers, taller than Sprout. Thimble keeps it under lock and key. I have asked every year for fifteen years to take it home. Fifteen nos. She is very consistent.
    - Old Bellamy Stroud cast me fifteen years ago, after three seasons as the back end of a mule. He said I had a grandee's voice and a mule's dignity. I have never had a better review.
    - My son. He plays the urchin who cheers for Juna in the first scene, and he steals it every year. He has learned every part in the play by accident. I raised him backstage. It shows, gloriously.
    - Farewell! Exit, pursued by applause!
